```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(adempR)
```

Simulation studies are easy to tune after the fact: a scenario that makes a
favored method look poor can be dropped, a measure can be swapped, a
failure rule can be changed. Pawel, Kook and Reeve (2024) show that these
choices can make any method appear superior. adempR therefore records the
design as data, fingerprints it, and records every later change.

## The protocol

`sim_protocol()` holds the reasoning behind each ADEMP choice. Fields that
are not given are reported as missing by `sim_completeness()`, which is a
checklist modeled on the reporting items of Williams et al. (2024) and the
preregistration template of Siepe et al. (2024).

```{r}
protocol <- sim_protocol(
  purpose = "method_comparison",
  scope = "Mean and median as estimators of a center; symmetric distributions, n from 20 to 200",
  dgm_rationale = "t distributions span normal to very heavy tails",
  estimand_rationale = "The center of symmetry is the target for all methods",
  method_rationale = "Mean and median are the usual default choices",
  measure_rationale = "Bias, empirical SE and coverage of nominal 95% intervals",
  replication_rationale = "Coverage MCSE at most 0.005",
  precision_targets = c(coverage = 0.005))
```

## Factorial designs

`sim_scenarios()` crosses its arguments. Values can be numbers, strings,
logicals or lists (for matrices or other objects).

```{r}
grid <- sim_scenarios(n = c(20L, 200L), df = c(3, 30))
as.data.frame(grid)
```

### Constraints

Not every combination is meaningful. A constraint of type `"exclude"`
removes scenarios deliberately and records why. A constraint of type
`"invalid"` marks combinations that must never occur, and stops with an
error if they do.

```{r}
grid2 <- sim_scenarios(n = c(10L, 100L), p = c(2L, 20L),
  .constraints = list(sim_constraint(function(s) s$n < 5 * s$p,
                                     "fewer than 5 observations per predictor")))
grid2$excluded
```

### Nested and sampled designs

When one factor only makes sense at some levels of another, bind separate
grids:

```{r}
nested <- sim_scenarios_bind(
  sim_scenarios(design = "parallel", clusters = 20L),
  sim_scenarios(design = "stepped_wedge", clusters = c(12L, 24L), steps = c(3L, 6L)))
as.data.frame(nested)
```

When the design space is too large to cross, sample from it and record the
sampling distribution:

```{r}
sampled <- sim_scenarios_sample(
  function() list(n = sample(20:500, 1), effect = round(runif(1, 0, 1), 2)),
  n = 6, seed = 1, distribution = "n uniform on 20:500; effect U(0, 1)")
as.data.frame(sampled)
```

Weights let summaries average over scenarios, for example to reflect how
often each setting occurs in practice (`sim_summarise(run, weighted = TRUE)`).

## Validation, freezing and amendments

`sim_validate()` checks that every method targets a declared estimand, that
methods only ask for scenario fields that exist, that the generator's own
checks pass in every scenario, and that every truth can be computed.

```{r}
study <- sim_study("center", protocol = protocol,
  scenarios = grid,
  generate = function(scenario, context) rt(scenario$n, scenario$df),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("center", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 0))),
  methods = list(mean = function(data) sim_estimate("center", mean(data)),
                 median = function(data) sim_estimate("center", median(data))),
  measures = c("bias", "empse"))
sim_completeness(study)[1:6, ]
```

Once the protocol is agreed, freeze it. The fingerprint covers the
generator, scenarios, estimands, truth, methods and evaluation choices.
Later changes need `sim_amend()` with a reason, and are recorded with the
fingerprints before and after.

```{r}
frozen <- sim_freeze(study)
amended <- sim_amend(frozen, alpha = 0.01, reason = "stricter test level agreed with reviewers")
amended$amendments[[1]][c("reason", "after_freeze")]
```

The report produced by `sim_report()` lists every amendment, so readers can
see which choices were made before and after results were seen.
